title: Constant versus completed integral coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with ring of integers $\cO_E$ and chosen uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Work on the small pro-étale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $R=(\cO_E)_X$ and $R_n=(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ for the constant sheaves of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and put
$$B=\cO_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R_n$$
with its canonical map $c:R\to B$; the identification with the pulled-back integral coefficient sheaf is [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Use the unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived extension of scalars [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $S=R$ or $B$, derived $\pi_E$-completeness means that the canonical map
$$M\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(M\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}R_n)$$
is an isomorphism; for $S=B$ this is [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. The canonical completion map and sequential derived limit use the functorial strict-tower model fixed in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]; its underlying homotopy limit is as in [def-weil-derived-limit].

1. $c$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and for every $n\geq1$ it induces an isomorphism
$$R_n=R/\pi_E^nR\xrightarrow{\sim}B/\pi_E^nB.$$
2. Restriction of scalars along $c$ is an equivalence from the derived $\pi_E$-complete objects of $D(B)$ onto the derived $\pi_E$-complete objects of $D(R)$, with inverse $L\mapsto$ derived completion of $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L$.
3. For every $K\in D(B)$ and every $n\geq1$, the canonical finite-reduction comparison is an isomorphism
$$K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}R_n\cong (\operatorname{Res}_c K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R_n$$
in $D(R_n)$.

proof.text: Extract the principal-ideal-ring clause for the recorded coefficient integer ring from extension_integers_dvr. The resulting Noetherian instance transports through ULift.ringEquiv. No condition on X is used.

Apply ConstantCompletion.flat_and_quotients on the coefficient-sized site. Transport its monoidal flatness assertion through siteSheafTensorRightIso to IsFlatOnSite. For each Boolean coefficient choice use its sectionwise quotient surjectivity and kernel formula. The image of the principal ideal (t)^k under the section ring homomorphism is (image(t)^k), by Ideal.map_span and Ideal.span_singleton_pow. This gives the required principal kernels. A zero quotient section restricts to zero on the maximal sieve; conversely local kernel membership implies the quotient vanishes locally, hence globally by sheaf separatedness.

Take finiteComparison and its chosen pure-tensor normalization from finiteComparison_existsUnique. Take the inverse of finiteDerivedComparison. Its inverse morphism is the original comparison morphism, so its computation equation is exactly the required equation, retaining the finite coefficient action.

Use koszul_quotient_reflector with the single given uniformizer generator on each coefficient ring. Its unit-isomorphism criterion identifies Complete with IsComplete. Rewrite the full subcategories by these equalities and apply ConstantCompletion.equivalence; its specified restriction isomorphism gives the first natural isomorphism.

Use the normalized sheafRingDerivedCoefficientAdjunction with the ordinary and homotopy-derived pairs supplied by derivedChangeOfRingsIndependentCoefficients. Precomposition by the homotopy quotient is fully faithful on natural transformations, so transports the right-Kan universal property to complexes. Transport through quotientCompQhIso and the ordinary-functor identification. Uniqueness of the right Kan extension identifies the resulting left adjoint with the specified extend; its right adjoint is definitionally dres. The completion reflector gives an adjunction from completion, lifted to complete objects, to their inclusion: the Hom equivalence is precomposition with completionUnit. Compose this adjunction with derived scalar extension and restrict along the fully faithful complete-object inclusion, using the restriction isomorphism of the equivalence. Uniqueness of left adjoints then identifies the equivalence inverse with completed derived scalar extension, naturally.
